body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER doc still mentions a case that no longer rejects**

The comment says a rename rejects with this marker when the id no longer names a media file, giving "already renamed by a double commit" as an example. That was true before this PR. Now `renameItem` finds the item by `assetId` under the names lock (`resolveTarget` → `resolveIdentity`, library-vault.ts:497-499), so a second commit follows the item to its new name and does not reject. It only throws `ItemNotFoundError` when no item has that `assetId` any more. `electron-api.ts:227` already describes this correctly ("Rejects when no item has `assetId`"). Suggest rewording this comment to match it, and the same for `ItemNotFoundError` at library-vault.ts:95.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: renameItem doc says a failed title write throws ItemNotFoundError, but the fs error is rethrown as is**

The docstring says `renameItem` "Throws `ItemNotFoundError` for an id without media, or when even the title cannot be written." But the title write at line 417 (`await atomicWriteFile(oldSidecar, …)`) has no try/catch. On a read-only vault or a locked sidecar the raw fs error (EACCES, EPERM, …) is rethrown without the `ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER`. Either wrap that write so it matches the doc, or change the doc to say a failed title write rethrows the underlying error. Callers that use the marker to tell "gone" apart from other failures depend on this.

🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: If the app crashes after allocateId, the stub sidecar is never cleaned up and its stem stays taken**

`allocateId` writes a stub sidecar (with a fresh `assetId`) before the media exists. Failures are handled: `vault.remove(id)` runs when the move fails (line 204), and screenshot-save.ts and stranded-recordings.ts do the same. A crash or kill between the allocation and `moveFile` is not handled, though. It leaves `.kaipu/<stem>.json` with no media and no `localRemovedAt`. `isStemFree` treats such an orphan sidecar as a cloud-only item (library-vault.ts:268-271), so the stem stays reserved for good. Stranded recovery then brings the take back under "… (recovered)" and never reclaims or removes the stub. One option is to mark stubs (for example `pendingSince`) and sweep stale ones during `recoverStrandedRecordings`.

🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The case-only rename test never runs the case-insensitive branch on Linux CI**

The test uses a temp directory from `mkdtemp(tmpdir())`. On Linux that directory is case-sensitive, so `isStemFree("Demo")` is true and `resolveRenameTarget` returns `mode: "free"` at `library-vault.ts:337`. It never reaches the `mode: "case"` / `moveInPlace` branch at `library-vault.ts:338-339`, which exists for APFS and NTFS. The test passes on CI, but the branch its name describes is untested there. To cover that branch everywhere, you could stub `isStemFree`/`isSameFile` so the folded name reads as taken by the same file, or add a test that runs only on a case-insensitive filesystem.

🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Roundabout file name expression in the media-URL test**

`` `${id}.mp4`.replace(".mp4", " clip.mp4") `` just produces `` `${id} clip.mp4` ``. Writing that directly would be easier to read. The test also looks up `` `${id} clip` `` a few lines further down.

🟠📝 **Fix · docs: ADR index says "nothing implemented yet" for an ADR this PR implements**

This index row lists ADR 0032 as "Proposed — design NIW2-560, nothing implemented yet". That isn't true. The ADR's own status table (0032 line 12) says it is implemented on this branch with acceptance pending owner QA, and this PR ships the implementation. Change the row to match, for example "Proposed — implemented, owner QA + manual Windows test pending". Row 0031 uses the same wording.

🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Gotcha leaves out the ambiguous-identity rejection**

This gotcha says a rename rejects only for an unknown id (`ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER`) or a title that cannot be written. The same page contradicts it at line 112, which says `AmbiguousIdentityError` is thrown before anything changes, and so does ipc-contract.mdx line 88, which lists `AMBIGUOUS_IDENTITY_MARKER` and invalid arguments as rejections. The renderer also handles that case with its own toast. Add the ambiguous-identity case (and invalid arguments) here so a reader doesn't assume the renderer only needs to handle not-found.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: §4–§5 contract blocks describe an API the later change-log entries replaced**

The code blocks in the spec body still show `renameLocalRecording(id: string, title: string)` (line 269), a handler that takes only `id`/`title` (lines 275–281), `renameItem(id, title, …)` (line 211) and `RenameKeptReason = "locked" | "busy" | "io"` (line 184). The code that shipped is `renameLocalRecording(id, assetId, title)` (`shared/types/electron-api.ts:230`) and `RenameKeptReason` now includes `"editing"` (`shared/types/library-storage.ts:80`). The §5.1 outcome table also has no rows for `editing` or the ambiguous-identity toast. The change log (lines 397–402) records each of these changes, so nothing here is hidden. But someone who reads §5 as the contract gets the wrong signature, and the header (line 8) says the spec is implemented. Consider adding a one-line "superseded, see change log / ipc-contract.mdx" note at the top of §4 and §5, or updating the signatures and the table in place.
Fixed in 81b80253: the marker doc now says it fires only when no item carries the requested assetId; a stale id follows the identity. — *Claude Code*

Fixed in 81b80253 by changing the doc, not the code: a failed title write rethrows the underlying fs error (EACCES, EPERM …). Wrapping it as ItemNotFoundError would make the renderer refresh quietly on a real write failure, which hides it. The doc also lists AmbiguousIdentityError now. — *Claude Code*

Agreed it can happen, deferring it on purpose. The cost of a crash between allocateId and the media move is a stub sidecar with no media, so the next capture with that name gets ' (2)'. No data is lost and the stub is invisible to list(). Telling a stub apart from a cloud-only sidecar (localRemovedAt) and sweeping it belongs with the reload reconciliation in NIW2-561 (https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-561/reconcile-the-library-with-files-changed-outside-the-app-on-reload); I added it to that ticket. — *Claude Code*

Fixed in 81b80253. The existing test is renamed '(any filesystem)' and says why on Linux it is a free move. A new test, 'takes the in-place branch on a case-folding filesystem (APFS/NTFS)', runs only where a probe shows the temp dir folds case, and asserts the folded stem is taken before the rename. It runs locally on macOS (3134 tests, +1). On Linux CI it is skipped, not falsely green. — *Claude Code*
Fixed in 81b80253: it now writes `${id} clip.mp4` directly. — *Claude Code*
Fixed in 81b80253: the row now reads 'Proposed — implemented, owner QA + manual Windows test pending'. — *Claude Code*

Fixed in 81b80253. The gotcha now lists every rejection: unknown identity (ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER), ambiguous identity (AMBIGUOUS_IDENTITY_MARKER, plain toast, nothing changes), invalid arguments, and a title write failure (fs error rethrown). — *Claude Code*

Fixed in 81b80253 with a note at the top of the spec. The §4–§5 blocks show the contract as first designed; the review rounds changed it (the change log lists how), and desktop/ipc-contract.mdx is authoritative. The spec is a design record, so I left its body as written rather than rewriting history. — *Claude Code*
